title: Data Lakehouse & Modern ETL Architecture
description: Explore Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg, ACID transactions on object storage, and ELT transformations.

questions.question: Which ACID property guarantees that a database transaction is either fully completed or completely rolled back?
options: Atomicity
Consistency
Isolation
Durability

questions.question: What is the key difference between ETL and ELT data processing pipelines?
options: In ELT, data is transformed inside the destination data warehouse after loading
In ELT, data is never stored in persistent storage
In ETL, data is loaded into memory without extraction
ELT can only handle uncompressed text files

questions.question: What architectural pattern combines the ACID transactions of data warehouses with the low-cost flexibility of data lakes?
options: Data Lakehouse
Monolithic Data Silo
Flat File Staging Area
Raw Blob Cache

questions.question: Why is Apache Parquet preferred over CSV for analytical queries?
options: It stores data columnarly with dictionary encoding, enabling high compression and column projection pushdown
It is plain human-readable text that can be viewed in notepad
It automatically prevents all duplicate primary keys without index overhead
It requires zero CPU deserialization time

questions.question: What problem does table partitioning solve in large distributed datasets?
options: It allows query engines to skip reading irrelevant data directories (partition pruning)
It replaces the need for data backups
It automatically converts relational data into GraphQL APIs
It forces all queries to run in single-thread memory
